_note: E3's transition-cost floor: the Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) National Employment Standards minimum notice (s117) and redundancy pay (s119) tables — real, federal, and the same for every award or EBA unless that instrument's own terms improve on them. Long service leave is deliberately not modelled here: it is state-based in Australia, not federal, and a single formula would be wrong for a majority of positions depending on jurisdiction — it always reads 'not computable, confirm jurisdiction' instead of a guessed figure.
instrument: Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) ss117, 119 (National Employment Standards)

noticeOver45Bonus.note: An extra week applies if the employee is over 45 with at least 2 years' continuous service. Atlas has no age field, so this bonus is never applied — the notice figure is therefore a floor, not a ceiling.

redundancyWeeksByTenureNote: The NES table genuinely drops from 16 to 12 weeks at the 10-year mark — not a typo, a real feature of s119. NES redundancy pay assumes an employer that is not a 'small business employer' (fewer than 15 employees), which is exempt from NES redundancy pay entirely; this engine assumes the establishment is not exempt unless told otherwise.
